Microservice scheduling

TraDE

Network- and traffic-aware adaptive scheduling for microservices operating under changing conditions.

IEEE TPDS · 2026·Published
Read paperExplore code
On this pageThe problemMy contributionDesign decisionsEvaluationLimitationsPaper & resources

The problem

Microservice response time depends on how much services communicate and the network paths between their hosts. Workload and network changes can make an initially reasonable placement expensive.

My contribution

I developed an adaptive scheduling approach that brings measured inter-service traffic and node-to-node network delay into placement decisions, subject to resource constraints.

Design decisions

Model communication in both directions

Request and response traffic may be asymmetric. Treating both directions explicitly gives the placement objective a more useful picture of communication cost.

Adapt to observed service performance

Use response-time behavior to identify when the current placement needs reconsideration, then evaluate feasible scheduling changes.

Keep placement decisions executable

Connect the scheduling algorithm to Kubernetes deployment controls and validate its effects with application-level performance measurements.

Evaluation & outcomes

In the evaluated DeathStarBench Social Network scenarios on a ten-node Kubernetes cluster, TraDE reports up to 48.3% lower average response time than NetMARKS under changing request patterns and controlled node delays. This is the largest improvement in the tested scenarios, rather than an expected result for every deployment.

48.3%maximum reduction in average response time vs. NetMARKS

What the results depend on

Moving services also has a cost. Placement benefits depend on traffic measurements, the duration of network changes, available capacity, and the operational effect of migration.
